sentences.text: The petition is filed under Section 482 of the Code of Criminal Procedure Code, 1973 seeking of the quashment of FIR being No.C.R.I-9 of 2016 registered with Modasa Rural Police Station District-Aravalli for the offences punishable under Sections 376, 506(2) and 114 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860.

2. Heard learned advocate Mr. Vivek B. Gupta for the petitioners and learned APP Ms. Monali H.
Bhatt for the respondent-State.
NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.MA/3750/2016 ORDER DATED: 08/10/2024 undefined 3.

The brief facts of the case are as under:-
3.1.

On 16.07.2015, the complainant-Harshidaben Patel entered into customary divorce with Paragkumar Mohanbhai Patel, who is claimed to be the husband of the Harshidaben Patel, for this, divorce deed has been executed between the complainant Sahilkumar Maheshbhai Patel vs State Of Gujarat on 8 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/142693652/
1 and her alleged husband.
On 07.08.2015, the complainant married with the petitioner No.1 as per the Hindu rites and rituals.
An affidavit relating to the said marriage was also executed between petitioner No.1 and complainant.
A Special Criminal Application (Habeas Corpus) being No.4674 of 2015 came to be filed by Paragkumar Mohanbhai Patel before this Court, the said application was disposed of.

sentences.text: On 10.08.2015, as victim expressed her wish to return to her parents home.

Thereafter, a complaint was filed by opponent against Paragkumar Mohanbhai Patel and FIR being FIR No.II-3142 of 2015 was registered with Modasa Rural Police Station offences punishable under Sections 323, 504, 506(2) and 114 of the NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.MA/3750/2016 ORDER DATED: 08/10/2024 undefined Indian Penal Code.
Opponent left the house of the petitioner No.1 and pursuant thereto, a missing complaint was lodged by the petitioner No.1 with Modasa Rural Police Station.

Thereafter, petitioner No.1 filed an application under Section 97 of the Criminal Procedure Code,
1973 for issuance of search warrant.
The said application was rejected by the learned trial Court.
4. Learned advocate for the petitioners has submitted that the allegations made in the FIR are absurd and improbable in view of certain facts, which can be seen from the record.

It is further submitted that in the FIR, it is the allegation of the victim that she married with one Paragkumar Mohanbhai Patel on 07.11.2014 and thereafter, she was taken back by her parents and family members.

It is further submitted that pursuant to a deed of dissolution of marriage executed between Paragkumar Mohanbhai Patel and the victim on 16.07.2015, victim got divorce from Paragkumar Mohanbhai Patel.

It is further NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.MA/3750/2016 ORDER DATED: 08/10/2024 undefined submitted that thereafter, on 07.08.2015, victim got married with accused No.1 Sahilkumar Maheshbhai Patel and she lived with the accused for one month and thereafter, on false allegations, a complaint is filed.

It is further submitted that after the victim eloped with Paragkumar Mohanbhai Patel, the present petitioner No.1 filed an application on 01.01.2016 under Section 97 of the Code of Criminal Procedure seeking a search warrant.

The statement of victim was recorded by the learned 3 rd Judicial Magistrate First class on 01.11.2016,
the victim has, in clear terms, stated that she is ready and willing to go back with Paragkumar Mohanbhai Patel.
The said application came to be dismissed on 11.01.2016.
It is further submitted that immediately, thereafter, on 14.01.2016, impugned FIR is registered on a false allegation.
It is further submitted that no offence is made out against the petitioner No.1.
It is further submitted that the case of the petitioner No.1 falls within the exception carved out in Section 375(2) of the Indian Penal Code.

It is further submitted that the victim and the petitioner NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.MA/3750/2016 ORDER DATED: 08/10/2024 undefined No.1 got married on 07.11.2015.
4.1.

In support of his submission, learned advocate for the petitioners has placed reliance upon the decision in the case of State of Haryana v. Bhajan Lal, reported in 1992 Supp (1) SCC 335 and has submitted that the present petition falls within clause No.1, 5 and 7, which are referred in paragraph No.104 of the said decision.

sentences.text: Per contra, learned APP for the respondent-State has vehemently objected and placed on record the certificate dated 02.02.2016 issued by Dr. Jalpa J. Chaudhari, M.D. Gynaec of Dr. Rasiklal Shah Sarvajanik Hospital, Modasa, which is taken on record.

Learned APP has also placed on record the copy of the statement of the victim dated 15.01.2016, which was recorded by the learned 3rd Judicial Magistrate First Class, Modasa, which is also taken on record.

It is submitted by the learned APP that as per the say of the victim, the alleged marriage with the petitioner No.1 was against her wish and the NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.MA/3750/2016 ORDER DATED: 08/10/2024 undefined age of the petitioner No.1 was under age at the relevant point of time.

It is further submitted that in the FIR it is also specifically alleged that against her wish, the petitioner No.1 had physical relations and petitioner Nos.2 and 3 threatened her not to leave the house.

It is further submitted that very serious offence has been committed by the petitioners and the medical report as well as the statement of the victim establishes the commission of the offence, hence, the learned APP would pray for dismissal of the petition.

6. Having heard the submissions advanced by the learned advocates for the respective parties and also on perusal of the FIR, it transpires that the allegations made by the victim is that victim got married with Paragkumar Mohanbhai Patel on 07.11.2014 and thereafter, at the instance of her parents and family members, a divorce deed was executed on 16.07.2015 between Paragkumar Mohanbhai Patel and the victim, whereby coupled got divorce.

It also transpires that when the victim was NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.MA/3750/2016 ORDER DATED: 08/10/2024 undefined sent with petitioner No.1, she informed the petitioner No.1 that she is already married to Paragkumar Mohanbhai Patel.
However, against her wish and consent, petitioner No.1 had intercourse with her.

It also transpires from the statement dated 15.01.2016, which was recorded before the learned Magistrate that petitioner No.1 has committed an offence punishable under Sections 376 of Indian Penal Code.

Even a statement is made by victim before the Medical Examiner that as petitioner No.1 was underage, her parents did not do marriage with him and only sent victim to petitioner No.1's home without marriage and petitioner No.1 had repeated intercourse with her against her wish and consent.
In catena of decisions, it has been observed that the FIR is not an encyclopedia of the commission of offence.

When prima facie on reading of the FIR, Court found that the petitioners are involved in the commission of offence, the FIR cannot be quashed and set aside, more particularly, when the heinous and serious offence has been alleged to have been committed by the petitioner No.1 in connivance with the NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.MA/3750/2016 ORDER DATED: 08/10/2024 undefined petitioner Nos.2 and 3, this Court is of the view that petition deserves to be dismissed.

It also transpires that there is nothing on record,
prima facie, to establish that the marriage between the petitioner No.1 and victim was solemnized as per the Hindu Rites and Ceremonies, except the statement made in the FIR.

Even the learned advocate for the petitioners could not point out from the record any material to establish that the marriage was solemnized between the victim and petitioner No.1, therefore, the provisions of Section 375(2) of the Indian Penal Code are not applicable to the facts of the present case.
Resultantly, the petition is dismissed.
No order as to costs.
